options: Whether a specific column value equals a literal
Whether the subquery's result is sorted
Whether the subquery returns at least one row, regardless of what columns it selects
Whether the outer table has more rows than the subquery
questions.explain: EXISTS only tests for the presence of at least one matching row — the actual columns selected inside it (often just SELECT 1) are irrelevant.

questions.q: What does `NOT EXISTS` return for a supplier with zero matching invoice rows?
options: True — the supplier is included in the result
False — the supplier is excluded
An error
NULL
questions.explain: NOT EXISTS is true when the inner subquery finds no matching rows, which is exactly the case for a supplier with zero invoices.

questions.q: Why is `NOT IN` risky when the subquery's column can contain NULL values?
options: NOT IN always raises a syntax error with NULLs present
NOT IN automatically converts NULLs to zero
There is no risk — NOT IN handles NULLs the same as NOT EXISTS
If even one row in the subquery's result is NULL, NOT IN silently returns zero rows for the entire query
questions.explain: NOT IN is implemented using <> comparisons internally, and comparing anything to NULL is never true, so a single NULL in the list poisons the whole result.

questions.q: Why doesn't NOT EXISTS have the same NULL problem as NOT IN?
options: NOT EXISTS ignores NULL values automatically by converting them to empty strings
NOT EXISTS only tests whether a matching row exists via its WHERE condition, so a stray NULL elsewhere in the subquery's result doesn't corrupt the comparison
NOT EXISTS cannot be used with any subquery that references NULL-able columns
They behave identically and both have the same NULL risk
questions.explain: NOT EXISTS is a presence test based on the join condition inside the subquery, not a value-list comparison, so NULLs elsewhere don't break it.

questions.q: When might you prefer a LEFT OUTER JOIN with IS NULL over NOT EXISTS for a 'missing record' question?
options: Never — NOT EXISTS is always strictly better
When the subquery might contain NULLs
When you also need to select columns from the right-hand table for the matched rows in the same query
LEFT OUTER JOIN cannot be used for missing-record questions at all
questions.explain: An outer join lets you pull additional columns from the joined table for matched rows in the same result, which a plain NOT EXISTS presence test does not provide.
